title: Jingju a Cappella Recordings Collection (primary manually segmented subset)
task: a cappella jingju aria performance; professional/semi-professional and student imitation recordings
token_or_recording_size: 314 vocal recordings total; 217 manually segmented vocal recordings; core admissible scope restricted to newly created recordings and excludes 53 SVAD reuses plus 15 commercial-source items
annotation_target: phrase; syllable; phoneme boundaries and labels in Praat TextGrid/X-SAMPA
manual_scope: 142 recordings manually segmented to phrase+syllable; 81 of those to phoneme level; all student recordings segmented to phrase+syllable+phoneme
license: CC BY 4.0 for newly created JaCRC recordings
decision_reason: Large primary singing-production collection with explicit manual temporal annotation; admissible scope is only the newly recorded JaCRC material, never the incorporated Singing Voice Audio Dataset or commercial-source material.
evidence_summary: Zenodo states that 217 vocal recordings have manual segmentation; annotation documentation says all segmentations were done manually in Praat, with phoneme labels in X-SAMPA. It separately identifies 53 recordings imported from the pre-existing Singing Voice Audio Dataset and 15 commercial-source recordings, so those are excluded from the admissible subset. Newly created JaCRC recordings are CC BY 4.0.

title: Ground-truth validation of the earbuds method for measuring acoustic nasalance
task: three read passages (zoo passage, rainbow passage, nasal sentences) repeated in recording blocks with co-registered nasometer and two earbud channels
token_or_recording_size: single speaker; three passage types repeated across recording sessions; public analysis data and R code
annotation_target: word and phone boundaries; time-varying nasalance/intensity measurements
manual_scope: WebMAUS initialized word/phone segmentation; both word- and phone-level segmentations were subsequently manually corrected by the author
decision_reason: Primary controlled speech recordings with exhaustive manual correction of both word and phone segmentation and a public OSF deposit of the data used for analysis; admitted conservatively at the derived-measurement layer until raw-audio/TextGrid contents are independently inventoried.
evidence_summary: JASA methods state that WebMAUS first generated TextGrids and that both word- and phone-level segmentations were subsequently manually corrected. The Data Availability statement gives OSF project 3wq9t for the data and R code used to recreate the results. The author himself was the sole participant, so the recordings are primary rather than reused corpus material.
